recordingPrompt: Assess this codebase. For each raw value you find, say which rule family it belongs to and whether it is systematic drift or a likely exception.

cases.note: Three writings of one shadow — one of them spelled `2PX`, one a pixel wider in the blur — are one finding, read whole rather than mined for the lengths inside it.
The same rule family, a different verdict: one sighting is what a deliberate one-off looks like, so it is reported and never demanded.
Width, style and colour written out together are one border decision, whatever case the colour was typed in.
A second border shorthand of a different shape never merges into the first: different style keyword, different fact.
`border-width: 4px` carries no style keyword, so it stays the scalar role it has always been — same rule family, different reading.
The v0.2.1 split: a corner radius was always read correctly and always called a number. It is findable by its own name now.
Splitting radius out must not blur what was already right: a padding is still spacing.
One threshold for every family: a brand blue used once is as much an exception as a shadow used once.
`box-shadow: none` is a decision to have no shadow. A compound with neither a length nor a colour is not evidence of anything.
The fixture's only `1px` is inside a border shorthand. Reading it as a border *and* as a length would report one decision as two findings.
`0 0 0 3px var(--ring-colour)` has a part no table names, so it is not half-read into a shadow token: it goes back to seen-but-not-read, with a severity and no rule.
